learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects of thermal engineering and fluid mechanics.
Have adequate knowledge of thermal engineering and fluid mechanics, including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field of mechanical engineering.
Ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve problems in thermal engineering and fluid mechanics using established methods.
Ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in thermal engineering and fluid mechanics.
Ability to perform bibliographic searches, use databases and other sources of information.
Ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods to solve problems in thermal engineering and fluid mechanics.
Ability to combine theory and practice to solve problems in thermal engineering and fluid mechanics.
Function effectively both individually and in a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Adequate knowledge of their branch of engineering, including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to perform bibliographic searches, use databases and other sources of information.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Function effectively both individually and in a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Water use in society (Industrial, commercial, residential)
Climate change, demographic factors and energy demand
Water to produce energy and energy to produce water
Water use in fossil fuel thermal plants
Water use in renewable energy plants
Relationships between water use, fuel type, operational efficiency, technology and environmental impact
Effects and consequences of water use in energy production
The water as a resource, demand pressure on water resources and energy generation
teaching_methods: Visit to a wastewater treatment plant
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade consists of 70% continuous assessment and 30% final exam. Continuous assessment includes four assignments (5% each), a laboratory report (20%), and a final project (30%). Both the final project and the final exam are mandatory to pass. For the extraordinary call, the assessment is based on a final project (50%) and a final exam (50%). The project is obligatory and must be submitted if not done in the ordinary call. A minimum grade of 4.5 out of 10 is required for extraordinary call components.
